title: ÆTHER: Storm Entry ending (Sitar and rubab)
story: After the drummers play for the hero, a new voice closes the scene as he rings the temple bell.
script: 66 s: the festival is alive; the drummers keep playing and a lone musician on the temple steps picks up the hero's tune. 80 s: korvai as he rings the bell. 85 s: title card, the 3-note call rings out.

brief.notes: Jithesh 30 Oct 10:10: 'in the end introduce something else, a humming or acoustic guitar, piano or sitar; sitar will be better; or an instrument from Central Asia or Arabic.' New ending joined onto storm-entry-v3-drums-join at 66.1 s. Sitar and rubab version. Prompt mode.

prompt: A 22-second ENDING section of a mass hero entry film score, made to be joined onto a running track, so it starts INSTANTLY in the middle of the groove at full energy: no intro, no silence, no fade-in, no build from nothing. Exactly 112 BPM, C minor, a festival percussion groove led by a real tabla with thavil and mridangam, played close, natural and dry; a warm low synth bass under it. Written like a South Indian film composer: a whistle-able 5-note hero hook with gamakam slides, call and response, a korvai ending. From the first second, a real sitar plays the hero hook over the tabla groove, natural and close with meend slides, no echo; at about 6 s a real Afghan rubab answers each sitar phrase, bright and plucked, a Central Asian voice, and they trade phrases faster and faster, both natural and dry. 14-19 s: a korvai, one rhythmic phrase played three times by sitar, rubab and tabla together, landing on a clean final hit. 19-22 s: the sitar alone plays a rising 3-note call (root, minor third, fifth, last note bent upward) and lets it ring with one temple bell. No thunder, no rain, no booms, no EDM, no risers, no fade-out, no silence at the start.
